prompt: Which of these best reflects what "Cache Strategies and Invalidation" covers?
hints: Reread the first point of the lesson: "Cache-aside (application checks cache, falls back to database on a miss, then populates the cache) is the most common pattern and gives the application full control over caching logic"
explanation: Cache-aside (application checks cache, falls back to database on a miss, then populates the cache) is the most common pattern and gives the application full control over caching logic — that's the core idea this lesson builds from.

prompt: True or false: Write-through (writes go to the cache and database together) keeps the cache always current at the cost of slightly slower writes — appropriate when read freshness matters most
